newsitem.title: FRANCE: Eurotunnel for speculators only - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel for speculators only - analysts.

text.p: Eurotunnel SA/PLC shares tumbled for a second day on the Paris and London bourses on Wednesday and is now nothing more than a speculators' stock, analysts said.

"The stock's no longer worth anything. It could fall to one franc, two francs, fifty centimes, nothing would shock me," said one Paris-based analyst. "It could equally well rise to 10 francs," he said.

The Anglo-French channel Tunnel operator's stock dropped as low as 6.95 francs in early trading from eight francs at the open, and was hovering around 7.25 francs at 0955 GMT. In London it was off 14p at 91 pence.
Another Paris-based analyst said there was no telling what would happen to a stock which was impossible to put a value on "with the horizon of a net profit way out in the year 2010".
"As long as there's no profit it's hard to put a value on the share," said the analyst. "We saw it fall to four or five francs one time. There's no reason why that might not happen again."
"Frankly I do not know what it's worth. It'll remain a speculative stock," the analyst, who asked not to be identified, said.
Volume in the stock was heading for 10 million shares at 1015 GMT but traders said there were no particularly large individual trades behind the moves in Paris.
The stock started retrading in Paris on Tuesday, after it revealed details of its debt restructuring deal with creditor banks, at nine francs and slid 7.2 percent to close at 8.35 francs.
One analyst noted that the stock had fallen to a low of 4.80 francs on April 3 and had risen to nine francs amid speculation in advance of the debt restructuring plan.

The tumble on Tuesday with a volume of 20 million shares traded followed the detailing on Monday of the refinancing of Eurotunnel's 69.6 billion francs of junior-ranked bank debt after a year of complex negotiations with bankers.
The agreement gives Eurotunnel's banks 45.5 percent of the company's capital in a debt-for-equity deal which awards the shares to the banks at 10.40 francs each.
Analysts in Paris said on Tuesday the terms of the deal were disappointing and that the market had been looking for 12-15 francs.

Traders said on Wednesday the renewed fall -- which brought the stock near a floor limit of 6.80 francs at which trading would be temporarily suspended under Paris stock market rules -- was driven by the sinking-in of a bearish outlook for returns on the stock.

"People are really disappointed with the plan -- no abandoning of loans, 3.5 billion of financial costs a year," said one Paris trader. "We've worked it out -- to pay a dividend of one franc you'd need an operating result of 6.5 to seven billion francs a year, and that's not going to come overnight."
"The fundamentals are buried by the speculative," he added.
